network.tdhConsolidation.metadataDescrip: How 6529 treats up to four of your wallets as one for TDH: the rules, the transactions, and the tested analysis behind the design.
network.tdhConsolidation.title: Wallet consolidation
network.tdhConsolidation.intro: Consolidation lets one collector's wallets count as one for TDH and for their profile. From {date}, a consolidation can hold up to {limit} wallets. This page sets out the rules, the transactions involved and the analysis behind the design, including what it protects against and what it does not.
network.tdhConsolidation.rules.title: The rules
network.tdhConsolidation.rules.descripti: Consolidations are registered on the NFTDelegation contract. 6529 reads those registrations and groups the wallets.
network.tdhConsolidation.rules.pairs.bod: Each pair of wallets registers a Consolidation (use case 999) in both directions, on Any Collection or The Memes. Two wallets need 2 registrations, three need 6 and four need 12.
network.tdhConsolidation.rules.limit.bod: A consolidation holds up to {limit} wallets. A fourth wallet counts only when its links to the other three were registered in both directions on or after {date}.
network.tdhConsolidation.rules.newest.bo: Wallets are grouped from confirmed links, newest first. If a member completes a link with a new wallet, that newer link moves it out of its group. This is how you leave a group or pair a wallet with a different one.
network.tdhConsolidation.rules.collector: Every wallet in a consolidation can sign in as the profile, set its primary address and redirect its airdrops. Only consolidate wallets you control. Combining different people's wallets is against the rules.
network.tdhConsolidation.rules.expiry.bo: Consolidation registrations do not expire. A link lasts until one of its wallets revokes it.
network.tdhConsolidation.rules.effects.b: Holdings across the wallets combine for TDH, including full sets, seasons, Genesis/Nakamoto and Gradient boosts, and transfers between them keep their acquisition time. The wallets' profiles merge permanently: the handle and picture come from the profile with the highest CIC, then TDH. Changes reach TDH within minutes and fully at the next 00:00 UTC snapshot.
network.tdhConsolidation.add.title: Add a wallet in four transactions
network.tdhConsolidation.add.description: The contract's batchDelegations function registers up to five links at once, so each wallet signs one transaction. Wallets already in the group sign first and the new wallet signs last.
network.tdhConsolidation.add.step1: Wallets A, B and C each register one link to D, in any order and at any time. Nothing changes yet.
network.tdhConsolidation.add.step2: D signs last, with one batch to A, B and C. The group becomes four wallets in one step.
network.tdhConsolidation.add.why: If D signs first, the group splits until the last link lands. Each split re-runs the profile merge, and TDH-wave votes above the temporarily lower TDH are reduced and not restored.

network.tdhConsolidation.order.title: Try the signing order
network.tdhConsolidation.order.descripti: Wallets A, B and C are already consolidated and D is joining. Choose who signs first, second, third and fourth to see the groups after each transaction.

network.tdhConsolidation.order.signerC: Wallet C: one link to D

network.tdhConsolidation.order.safe: No temporary split. A, B and C stay together, and D joins with the last transaction.
network.tdhConsolidation.order.unsafe: The group split in {count} of {total} steps before D joined. Each split re-runs the profile merge and can reduce TDH-wave votes.
network.tdhConsolidation.order.note: This simulation uses the same grouping rule as the backend: newest confirmed link first, every member linked both ways, up to four wallets.
network.tdhConsolidation.remove.title: Remove or replace a wallet
network.tdhConsolidation.remove.leave: A wallet you still control leaves with one batchRevocations transaction that revokes its links to all the others at once.
network.tdhConsolidation.remove.replace: To replace a wallet in a group of two or three, add the new one first, then remove the old one, so the group never gets smaller. A group of four is full: remove the old wallet first, then add the new one. The other three stay consolidated in between.
network.tdhConsolidation.remove.lost: If a wallet's key is lost or compromised, every remaining wallet revokes its link to it, one transaction each. Send them back to back: the removed wallet keeps access to the profile until the last revocation lands.
network.tdhConsolidation.remove.split: When a consolidation splits, the part holding a primary address set at least 7 days earlier keeps the profile. Otherwise the part with the most TDH keeps it. TDH builds up over days held, so a newly compromised wallet cannot quickly outweigh your others.
network.tdhConsolidation.why.title: Why every pair: the alternatives we tested
network.tdhConsolidation.why.description: Asking every pair to link both ways costs a few transactions. Cheaper rules were modelled and tested before choosing.
network.tdhConsolidation.why.table.capti: Rules considered for the fourth wallet
network.tdhConsolidation.why.rule.majori: Linked both ways with any two members
network.tdhConsolidation.why.rule.fanout: Links to all members, one member approves
network.tdhConsolidation.why.problem.maj: Two of your wallets could add an outside wallet without the third.
network.tdhConsolidation.why.problem.fan: One wallet's key, or one transaction it was tricked into signing, could add an outside wallet to your full consolidation without anything visibly changing.
network.tdhConsolidation.why.problem.sin: The same weakness, and linking a member with a new wallet would pull the new wallet in instead of moving the member out, changing what that action means today.
network.tdhConsolidation.why.matrix.titl: Who can add an outside wallet to your consolidation?
network.tdhConsolidation.why.matrix.desc: An attacker owns an outside wallet and can make some of your wallets sign. The table shows whether the outside wallet can join your full consolidation, found by trying every set of registrations those wallets could sign.
network.tdhConsolidation.why.matrix.capt: Whether an outside wallet can be added, by rule and by how many of your three wallets an attacker controls
network.tdhConsolidation.why.conclusion: Every pair is the only rule where no subset of your wallets can add an outside wallet, and where every member follows the same rule. The cheapest alternative saves two transactions, once.
network.tdhConsolidation.protects.title: What consolidation protects, and what it does not
network.tdhConsolidation.protects.adding: No subset of your wallets can add an outside wallet: every existing wallet has to sign, and so does the new one.
network.tdhConsolidation.protects.old: Old registrations cannot fill the fourth slot. Links registered before the start date never form a group of four.
network.tdhConsolidation.protects.keys: It does not make any one wallet safer. Each wallet in a consolidation is a full key to your profile: if one is compromised, the attacker can sign in, change the primary address and redirect airdrops, whatever the consolidation rule. Four wallets means four such keys.
network.tdhConsolidation.protects.manage: A delegation manager (use case 998) can register and revoke consolidations for the wallet that appointed it. If one manager acts for all your wallets, that manager's key is enough to change your consolidation.
network.tdhConsolidation.protects.lock: A vault can refuse new consolidation links, including ones its manager sends, by locking use case 999 on Any Collection. It has to unlock before its consolidation can change.
network.tdhConsolidation.start.title: Why the fourth wallet has a start date
network.tdhConsolidation.start.body: Some wallets registered consolidation links long ago, for other reasons. If the limit had simply changed, those old links could have formed groups of four the moment it did. Counting a fourth wallet only for links registered from {date} means every group of four is set up on purpose under the new rule. Requiring both directions means an old one-sided registration cannot be completed by the other wallet alone.
network.tdhConsolidation.start.data: On {snapshotDate} there were {total} consolidations of two or more wallets: {two} of two and {three} of three. With the start date, none of them change when the limit rises. Without it, {ungated} would have changed straight away.
network.tdhConsolidation.tested.title: How it was tested
network.tdhConsolidation.tested.port: The backend grouping code was copied into a test harness and checked against all {total} live consolidations, with identical results.
network.tdhConsolidation.tested.exhausti: Each rule was checked exhaustively: every set of registrations an attacker controlling some of your wallets could sign, and every order in which a new wallet's transactions can land.
network.tdhConsolidation.tested.properti: Property tests check that {graphs} random wallet graphs group exactly as before when no registration is after the start date, and that {sequences} random register-and-revoke sequences keep the stored links consistent.

network.tdhConsolidation.faq.title: Questions
network.tdhConsolidation.faq.friend.titl: Can I consolidate with a friend or another collector?
network.tdhConsolidation.faq.friend.body: No. Consolidation is for one collector's wallets. Every wallet becomes a full key to the profile, and combining different people's TDH is against the rules.
network.tdhConsolidation.faq.before.titl: I registered four wallets before the start date. What now?
network.tdhConsolidation.faq.before.body: Your consolidation keeps three of them, as before. From {date}, register the fourth wallet's links again in both directions, one transaction per wallet with the fourth wallet last, and it will join.
network.tdhConsolidation.faq.tdh.title: Does adding a fourth wallet change my TDH?
network.tdhConsolidation.faq.tdh.body: Its holdings join yours. They count toward full sets, seasons, Genesis/Nakamoto and Gradient boosts, and transfers between your consolidated wallets keep their acquisition time.
network.tdhConsolidation.faq.profile.tit: Which profile survives when wallets join?
network.tdhConsolidation.faq.profile.bod: The profiles merge permanently. The handle and picture come from the profile with the highest CIC, then the highest TDH.
network.tdhConsolidation.faq.order.title: What happens if I sign in the wrong order?
network.tdhConsolidation.faq.order.body: The consolidation splits until the last link lands. Each split re-runs the profile merge, and TDH-wave votes above the temporarily lower TDH are reduced and not restored. Re-cast them once the group is complete.
network.tdhConsolidation.faq.expiry.body: No. Expiry dates are ignored for consolidations. A link lasts until one of its wallets revokes it.
